land.text: Colchis, which Mithridates VI Eupator conquered

successors.note: Pontus page: Mithridates VI began 'his expansion by inheriting Lesser Armenia from King Antipater (precise date unknown, c.115-106) and by conquering the Kingdom of Colchis'. The year 110 is a bridge.

land.text: Colchis as Rome's client kingdom under Aristarchus (63-47), later Lazica/Egrisi

successors.note: Infobox 'Succeeded by: Lazica'. Not a direct hand-over: Pontus (c. 110-65) and Pompey's occupation (65) come between.

capitals.name: Aea (Kutaisi)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Aea'; the page glosses it 'Cyta or Cutatisium or Aia (now Kutaisi)'. The page does not date the seat within 301-110.

keyframe_review.note: 44,265 km2 for 301-282, bbox 39.63-44.98 E, 40.68-43.80 N (Georgia, Turkey, Russia). The Colchis page gives no area and no dates inside 301-231 (its only ruler dated there is Kuji, 325-280, and it says Colchis fragmented into royal governors, undated), so there is no infobox figure to compare. The page's extent fits the western bbox: Trabzon to the Rioni with Samegrelo, Imereti, Guria, Adjara, Svaneti, Racha, Abkhazia and the Turkish provinces Rize, Trabzon and Artvin ('Lazistan'). The shape's east edge, 44.98 E, lies well beyond Svaneti and Racha (about 43.5 E); if it reaches Kartli it overlaps Iberia. Unverified within the page budget.
44,145 km2 for 281-240, same bbox as the 301 shape; the page is silent for these years (unverified: page budget).

44,145 km2 for 239-231, identical in area to the previous shape; the page is silent (unverified: page budget). Cliopatria ends Colchis in 231, but the Pontus page has the kingdom conquered by Mithridates VI, so the shape is carried on (next entry).

correction.text: carried on from the 231 shape until Mithridates VI 'conquer[ed] the Kingdom of Colchis' (undated; c. 115-106 is the page's range for his Lesser Armenian inheritance)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria drops Colchis in 231, yet the Pontus page treats it as a kingdom that Mithridates VI conquered (reign 120-63), and the Colchis page does not say the kingdom ended earlier. The 231 outline is bridged to c. 110 at low confidence; neither page dates the conquest or gives a border.

region.text: Colchis, the Black Sea coast from Trabzon to Abkhazia, with the Rioni basin

ledger.note: 301: Cliopatria's Colchis shape begins; the Colchis page is silent on 301-231. It dates the kingdom to 'the sixth century BC' (Cornell), lists Kuji as ruler 325-280, and says the Achaemenid-era tribes were organised into satrapy and tribute, with no year. The start year is Cliopatria's, a bridging judgment.

c. 110: Mithridates VI of Pontus conquers Colchis. 'Mithridates began his expansion by inheriting Lesser Armenia from King Antipater (precise date unknown, c.115–106) and by conquering the Kingdom of Colchis.' The page gives no year for Colchis; 110 is the middle of the Lesser Armenia range and matches the kingdom-of-pontus dossier's gain. The Colchis page adds that he 'quelled an uprising in the region in 83 BC' and gave Colchis to his son, so Colchis was Pontic by then.

wars.name: Mithridates VI's conquest of Colchis
wars.outcome: Colchis passes to the Kingdom of Pontus; a revolt there was put down in 83 BC and Colchis was given to the king's son Mithridates (Colchis page).
wars.note: Year bridged (page: undated; c. 115-106 for the Lesser Armenian inheritance in the same sentence). Pompey then occupied Colchis in 65 BC and installed Aristarchus (63-47), beyond this dossier's life.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey frontier is on the pages; Strabo's and Ptolemy's differing western limits (Trabzon, the Rioni) show the edge was approximate.

sources.title: Colchis
sources.note: Infobox (capital Aea, dates 13th c. BC to 131 AD), extent, Mithridates VI 83 BC, Pompey 65 BC; silent on 301-231 and on any area.

sources.title: Kingdom of Pontus
sources.note: Mithridates VI's conquest of Colchis (undated); silent on Colchis in the 3rd century.

notes: Cliopatria row Colchis has 3 shapes, 301-231, drawn as one 44,265 km2 outline; the two pages opened (budget 1-2) say nothing about Colchis between 301 and 231, so all three shapes are 'ok' but unverified, and the birth and death events are confidence 1. The row is extended to c. 110 (new keyframe) because the Pontus page treats Colchis as a kingdom conquered by Mithridates VI; the kingdom-of-pontus dossier records its c. 110 gain of Colchis against 'nobody' on the ground that no Cliopatria state holds Colchis after 231, which this dossier now contradicts: a reviewer should change that counterpart to colchis. The state's real life per the page runs from the sixth century BC (Cornell) with the 'Disestablished 131 AD' of the infobox; Lazica (Cliopatria row from 63) is the later state on the same land and may deserve one lazica dossier (see eu-19). Not used because outside this dossier's life: Pompey's occupation (65), Aristarchus (63-47), Polemon and Pythodorida, the Anicetus revolt (69 AD), Goths (253). Page figures not on a map: no area. Gazetteer: 'Colchis' resolves (Egrisi, Lazica, Western Georgia aliases).
